original_value: For a concurrent program, a prediction tool maps the history of a single run to a prediction of bugs in an exponential number of other runs. If all those bugs can occur, then the tool is sound. This is the case for some data race tools like RVPredict, but was, until now, not the case for deadlock tools. We present the first sound tool for predicting deadlocks in Java. Unlike previous work, we use request events and a novel form of executability constraints that enable sound and effective deadlock prediction. We model prediction as a general decision problem, which we show is decidable and can be instantiated to both deadlocks and data races. Our proof of decidability maps the decision problem to an equivalent constraint problem that we solve using an SMT-solver. Our experiments show that our tool finds real deadlocks effectively, including some missed by DeadlockFuzzer, which verifies each deadlock candidate by re-executing the input program. Our experiments also show that our tool can be used to predict more, real data races than RVPredict.

result.paraphrase: For concurrent programs, a prediction tool extrapolates the history of one execution to bug predictions over exponentially many other executions. The tool is sound if every such bug can happen. Some data-race tools, such as RVPredict, satisfy this property, but until now deadlock tools did not. We introduce the first sound Java deadlock prediction tool. In contrast to prior work, it relies on request events and a new kind of executability constraint to achieve sound and effective deadlock prediction. We formulate prediction as a general decision problem and prove it is decidable, with instances for both deadlocks and data races. To establish decidability, we reduce the decision problem to an equivalent constraint problem solved with an SMT solver. Experiments indicate that the tool detects real deadlocks effectively, including some that DeadlockFuzzer misses by re-executing the input program to validate each candidate. The experiments also show that it can predict more real data races than RVPredict.
